s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cerebellopontine angle syndrome with headache and neurologic deficits
salient_findings: Large lobulated mass at the left cerebellopontine angle
key_facts: 3-month history of worsening symptoms
Headache exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
Bilateral past-pointing on neurologic examination
Intention tremor on neurologic examination
6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm mass at the left cerebellopontine angle
Mass involves and expands Meckel’s cave
Mass contains multiloculated cystic areas and solid components
Compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
Dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
Anterior displacement of the cavernous sinus
Encasement and mild narrowing of the left petrous internal carotid artery

shortlist.label: Vestibular schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common tumor at cerebellopontine angle, matches symptoms

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Frequent tumor in this location, can cause similar neurologic deficits

shortlist.label: Trigeminal schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given involvement of Meckel's cave and extension into infratemporal fossa

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic components and location at cerebellopontine angle are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Cystic meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches imaging findings of multiloculated cystic areas and solid components

raw.rationale: The mass involves and expands Meckel’s cave, which is a common location for trigeminal schwannomas, and contains multiloculated cystic areas and solid components, consistent with the heterogeneous appearance of schwannomas on imaging.

rejected.label: Vestibular schwannoma
rejected.why: Typically centered at the internal auditory canal, which is not the primary location of the mass in this case

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: While meningiomas can have a similar appearance, the involvement of Meckel’s cave and the specific location at the cerebellopontine angle are more suggestive of a trigeminal schwannoma

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Typically appears as a homogeneous, T1-hypointense and T2-hyperintense lesion without solid components or enhancement, which does not match the heterogeneous appearance of the mass in this case

rejected.label: Cystic meningioma
rejected.why: While meningiomas can be cystic, the specific involvement of Meckel’s cave and the location at the cerebellopontine angle are more suggestive of a trigeminal schwannoma
